proof.text: Termwise extension from a commutative ring S to T preserves quasi-isomorphisms between S-K-flat complexes: use the proved scalarExtension_quasiIso_of_kFlat helper, which specializes mixedTensor_kFlat_quasiIso to the complex T in degree zero. For restriction from A to R followed by extension to B, use the ordinary tensor isomorphisms on P and Q. Their pure-tensor formulas give the commuting arrow square for any A-linear complex map. Extension from A to A tensor_R B preserves the K-flat quasi-isomorphism, and exact restriction to B preserves it; transport through that square.

For any additive module functor F preserving K-flat quasi-isomorphisms, form G=F.mapHomotopyCategory followed by Qh. Use as resolving class the homotopy objects represented by K-flat complexes. The chosen flat resolution and its augmentation establish the resolution hypothesis. The proved isIso_Qh_map_mapHomotopyCategory_map lemma gives the inversion hypothesis. Apply leftDerived_from_resolvingClass to obtain an exact, hence additive, derived functor L with counit invertible on the chosen resolutions.

Whisker the augmentation with the quotient and Qh. It is pointwise invertible because each augmentation is a quasi-isomorphism. Transport additivity of Qh composed with the quotient to the localized resolution, and compose with additive L. Whisker the derived counit with the resolution and quotient; its components are invertible by the resolving-class computation clause. Transport additivity again. Finally compose the natural homology factorization isomorphisms and mapHomotopyCategoryFactors, and transport additivity to resolution followed by termwise F and ordinary homology.

For source take F to be extension from R to B and precompose the generic additivity result with additive restriction from A to R. For target take F to be restriction from A to R followed by extension to B. The first step establishes both preservation hypotheses. Unfold the source and target functor definitions and assemble the two additive instances. No additivity of the chosen resolution is assumed.

title: Additivity of affine tensor cohomology
statement: For commutative R-algebras A and B, and every integer i, the source and target functors defined in [def-pc-ring-tensor-cohomology] are additive, with no flatness or boundedness hypotheses.
